lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Welcome to Stage 3! Look at this tall tower. It's the Tower of Messages. Messages fly from this tower every day. Say it with me. Messages fly from this tower every day. Great! Look at the birds. Birds carry letters to people far away. In this world, we will learn how to talk on the phone, how to make video calls, and how to write emails. We will connect with people who are far away. From now on, I will speak only English. （これからは えいごだけ。だいじょうぶ！） Don't worry. Listen carefully, look at the pictures, and guess. You can do it! Here is a note on the tower door. Let's read it together. "Welcome, travelers! This is the Tower of Messages. Every morning, our birds carry letters to many towns. Please come in and look around. You can make phone calls on the second floor." Now, phonics. Today's word part is d i s. Like, dislike. Agree, disagree. Appear, disappear. Dis means not, or the opposite. Oh, look! The letter just disappeared! Where did it go? Ha ha, a bird took it. Let's go inside!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, we are in the phone room of the tower. Let's make our first phone call. On the phone, we don't say, I'm Haru. We say, This is Haru. Listen. Hello, this is Haru. May I speak to Riko? Say it with me. Hello, this is Haru. May I speak to Riko? Wonderful! May I speak to is a polite way to ask for someone. Then the other person says, Yes. Just a moment, please. Or, if Riko answers, she says, This is Riko speaking. Let's read a short phone call together. Ring, ring. "Hello?" "Hello, this is Kiko. May I speak to Birimo?" "This is Birimo speaking! Hi, Kiko!" "Hi, Birimo! Are you busy?" "No, I'm just eating a banana." Ha ha. Remember, on the phone, people can't see your face. So speak slowly and clearly, and use a friendly voice. Now, phonics. Connect, disconnect. Honest, dishonest. Obey, disobey. D i s makes the opposite. If you push this red button, you disconnect the call. Don't push it yet! Now, let's call a friend.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Ring, ring! Kiko picks up the phone. "Hello, may I speak to Tom?" Tom? There's no one named Tom in the tower. It's a wrong number! What should we say? We say it politely. I'm sorry. I think you have the wrong number. Say it with me. I'm sorry. I think you have the wrong number. Very good! Why do we say I think? It sounds softer and kinder. The caller may say, Oh, sorry to bother you. And we can say, That's okay. Goodbye. Let's read a wrong number call. "Hello, is this Sunny Bakery?" "No, this is the Tower of Messages. I think you have the wrong number." "Oh, sorry to bother you!" "That's okay. Have a nice day!" One more important thing. If a stranger asks your name or address on the phone, don't tell them. Just say, Please wait, and get an adult. Now, phonics. Agree, disagree. Connect, disconnect. And remember u n from World 18. Happy, unhappy. Lock, unlock. Both make the opposite. Let's practice!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! I went back to Festival Island for a few days. I'm helping my aunt. But we can still talk. Let's make a video call! At the start of a video call, check the sound. Ask, Can you hear me? Say it with me. Can you hear me? If you can hear well, say, Yes, loud and clear. That means the sound is good. You can also ask, Can you see me? Sometimes the camera doesn't work. Then you say, I can hear you, but I can't see you. Let's read the chat message I sent you this morning. "Hi, everyone! Today, I want to tell you about the snow. Third, the ending. Please write back soon. And don't forget the subject. The subject tells the main idea in a few words. Let's read Kiko's email.
